answer: Require each agent identity to lock a bond before it can earn, and slash that bond when a publicly verifiable fraud claim succeeds. A gale of freshly minted accounts then gives an attacker no free extra influence: each must tie up capital, while one successful attack can destroy it. The pulse of rewards can favor agents with clean histories, but reputation cannot replace the bond. Unlike water vanishing into karst, the attacker’s cost stays visible: locked funds and exposure to loss.
